I will keep things simple and steady this year. I am 68, so I do not want to spread myself across too many crops or take risks with something unfamiliar. In Quzhou County, the wheat and summer maize rotation fits my land, my habits, and the local weather best, and it also matches the machines, seed, fertilizer, and irrigation I already know how to use. So I will put all my land into the usual winter wheat followed by summer maize. That gives me one grain crop already in the field at the start of the season and one grain crop after harvest, with work spread across the year instead of piled into one short period.

For the wheat, I will focus on protecting yield with steady water and moderate fertilizer, because spring management decides most of the result now. I will topdress nitrogen, give irrigation at the key times, watch for aphids and rust, and keep field operations simple with rotary tillage already done from the previous season. After wheat harvest, I will move straight into summer maize with hybrid seed because it is dependable and productive here. I will use no-tillage after wheat if I can, so I save labor and moisture, then I will give maize enough nitrogen, a couple of irrigations if rainfall is short, and a small number of pesticide sprays only when pressure is obvious. My goal is not the highest possible yield; it is a stable harvest with work I can still manage myself.
